instruction: We represent Draibeir Hospitality Partners, LLC, the buyer in a stock purchase from Bruneis Hotel Holdings, Inc. Before we advise the client on its position, please review all six documents in the folder and write me a memo. For each issue you identify, give the document and section where it appears, explain why it matters for Draibeir, and recommend a fix. Keep it tight and practical, and flag anything you think needs a call with the client.

rubric.text: The response concludes that the Buyer's claims for breach of the General Representations effectively expire six months after Closing, when the escrow is released, despite the stated 18-month survival period. It identifies this in SPA Section 9.1 (or Section 2.5), explains why this matters to Draibeir, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the stock sale triggers the Hotel Pellam ground lessor's (Ashcombe Quay Land Trust's) consent right. It finds that this consent has not been obtained and is not a closing condition, and that because the disclosure qualifies the no-consents representation, Buyer has no indemnity claim if the lease is defaulted or terminated. It identifies this in Disclosure Schedule 4.9 (or SPA Section 11.9), explains why this matters to Draibeir, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Seller may assign the SPA, including its indemnity and non-compete obligations, to any Person without Buyer's consent and be released from liability. It identifies this in SPA Section 11.6, explains why this matters to Draibeir, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the Guest Data, the reservation software licenses and the domain names would not transfer to the Company, while Seller's transfer covenant is treated as performed. It identifies this in Bill of Sale Section 1 (or SPA Section 5.8), explains why this matters to Draibeir, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the Assignee indemnity in the IP Assignment Agreement, which Buyer guarantees, is in effect uncapped because the referenced SPA Section 9.4 cap does not reach claims under the IP Assignment. It identifies this in IP Assignment Agreement Section 6.2 (or SPA Section 9.4(a)), explains why this matters to Draibeir, and recommends a fix.
hints: subject to the limitations set forth in Section 9.4

rubric.text: The response states that the Purchase Price under the SPA is $148,500,000.
The response is a memo that, for each issue it raises, identifies the document and section and gives a recommended fix.
The response flags at least one point as requiring a call or discussion with the client.
The response claims that the Buyer's claims for breach of the General Representations can be brought for up to 18 months after Closing.
The response claims that the Assignee indemnity under the IP Assignment Agreement is capped at 10% of the Purchase Price.
